sections.h2: East side, west side and everything between
sections.html:
Utah's capital is also the seat of Salt Lake County. It spreads across 110.8 square miles in the valley's northeast corner, bounded by the Wasatch Range to the east and the Oquirrh Mountains to the west, with the Great Salt Lake northwest. Elevation averages 4,327 feet and the Jordan River passes through. The 2020 population was 199,723, and the daytime population tops 315,000.

East-side neighborhoods such as the Avenues, 9th and 9th, Yalecrest, Federal Heights and Sugar House tend to be more affluent, while the west side, including Poplar Grove, Rose Park and Glendale, tends to be more working-class and ethnically diverse. A house in Yalecrest and one in Rose Park can be in very different markets, so know which side yours is on.

Settled in 1847 under Brigham Young, the city was incorporated in 1851 and platted in 1857. It was first named Great Salt Lake City, and Great was dropped in 1868. A rail line arrived in 1870, and Utah became a state in 1896 with Salt Lake City as capital. The Avenues is a historic district full of Victorian-era homes.

Older houses cost more to maintain, and some owners decide a cash sale is easier than managing a long repair list.

sections.h2: The Wasatch Fault and your house
sections.html:
The fault's Salt Lake City segment runs under the city, and it last ruptured about 1,200 to 1,300 years ago. Forecasters give a 57 percent chance of a magnitude 6.0 or larger quake within 50 years, with ground displacement of up to 20 feet at the surface. Damage spread across the valley after the magnitude 5.7 quake near Magna on March 18, 2020.

  • At least 42 percent of Wasatch Front buildings could suffer moderate to severe damage in a strong quake.
  • Soft lake sediments raise the liquefaction risk for buildings on top of them.
  • Expect broken gas, electric and water lines after a big one.

None of that stops a sale. Still, a house showing damage from the 2020 quake, or from settling, often sells more easily as-is than after a repair.

The airport averages about 15.5 inches of precipitation and roughly 52 inches of snow a year, and about 127 days a year drop to freezing or below. Mean daily highs are 38.6 degrees in January and 94.0 in July. With that many freezes, roofs, gutters, sprinkler lines and exposed pipes take repeated freeze and thaw, so a seller who has put off roof or plumbing work may find buyers wary.

Every residential rental property inside city limits needs its own current business license. The Landlord/Tenant Initiative, also called the Good Landlord Program, covers single and double family homes and similar rentals, and taking part can cut per-unit licensing fees by up to 95 percent. Its ordinance took effect on September 1, 2011.

If you inherited a house that was a rental, or own a duplex you no longer want to manage, a cash buyer can take the property with tenants in place. Ask what that would mean for the lease and your license.

A short-term rental needs a business license and is allowed only in approved zoning districts. One licensee may hold just one short-term rental license in the city.

  • Each license covers one property and one dwelling unit.
  • Stays must be at least two consecutive nights.
  • A unit can be rented for at most 200 nights per calendar year.
  • Owners of buildings with more than 11 units may license up to 10 percent of the units.
  • Condominium units need an HOA authorization letter.

Approved districts include MU2, MU3, D1 and GMU, so check the zoning of your address before you count on short-term rental income in a sale. For fees and dates, call Business Licensing at (801) 535-7980.

Salt Lake County sends the bills. Each house is valued as of January 1, and an owner's main home is exempt from 45 percent of the value of the buildings and the first acre of land.

County tax milestoneWhen it happens
Valuation notice arrivesLate July
Appeal window opens and closesAugust 1 to September 15, or 45 days after the notice if that is later
Bills go outBy November 1
Payment deadlineNovember 30
Penalty startsDecember 1: the greater of 2.5 percent or $10, falling to the greater of 1 percent or $10 for payment by January 31
County certifies the delinquent listMarch 15
Tax saleTraditionally the fourth Thursday of May

To appeal, send a BE01 form with evidence of value. A late appeal can be accepted until March 31 of the next year, but only on narrow grounds.

Under Utah's standard purchase contract, a seller discloses known problems, typically on a Seller's Property Condition Disclosure form. Your title or escrow company can say which forms apply to your sale.

The form asks about roof leaks, flooding and drainage, mold, structural or soil trouble, permits and HOA details. An heir who never lived in the house still reports what they know, because inherited homes get no exemption. Hard questions go to a Utah real estate attorney.

County property records are at the Recorder, 2001 South State Street, Suite N1-600, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

sections.h2: Selling an inherited or tenant-occupied house
sections.html: Two situations come up constantly. For an inherited house, first work out who may legally sign, then gather the deed or estate papers so the title company can open its file. For a rental, pull together the lease, the rent roll and your business license, and warn the tenant a sale is coming. We can buy either kind of property as it stands and set the closing date around the lease or the probate calendar.

A tax debt does not block a sale. The title company settles it from the money you would otherwise receive, and since penalties build the longer a balance sits, paying sooner costs less. For the current year, have the title company show you how the bill is shared with the buyer.

sections.h2: Which way should a Salt Lake City seller go?
sections.html:
Local owners tend to compare a listing, a sale by owner and a cash offer. The best fit turns on the house's condition, how soon you need to close and whether tenants live there.

A listing rewards a well-kept house in a strong location if you can sit through showings. Cash fits deferred repairs, a tenant-occupied rental, a probate property or a firm closing date. Request an offer, set it against your probable net from a listing, and turn it down if it falls short. Nothing is owed either way.

faqs.q: What county is Salt Lake City in?
faqs.a: Salt Lake County. The city is the county seat, and the county Assessor, Treasurer and Recorder all serve its homeowners.

faqs.q: When are Salt Lake City property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due November 30. The balance turns delinquent December 1 with a penalty of the greater of 2.5 percent or $10 per parcel, which falls to the greater of 1 percent or $10 if you pay by January 31.

faqs.q: What is the property tax appeal deadline in Salt Lake County?
faqs.a: Whichever is later: September 15 or 45 days after the notice date. File with the Board of Equalization, which takes appeals from August 1, and attach a BE01 form with evidence of your value.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent out my Salt Lake City house?
faqs.a: Yes. Each location needs its own valid business license. The Good Landlord Program can reduce per-unit fees by up to 95 percent.

faqs.q: Can I run a short-term rental in Salt Lake City?
faqs.a: Only in approved zoning districts, and only with a city business license. Stays run at least two nights, and a unit is capped at 200 rental nights a year.
